reader_question: How many people have private health coverage, public coverage, both, or neither?
grade_line: Official statistics: the Census Bureau’s American Community Survey
title: About 23.8 million Americans had both private and public health coverage in 2025, and 28.3 million had neither.
measure_line: People by health insurance coverage, millions, 2025, civilian noninstitutionalized population, United States
notes: The two circles are drawn the same size, so their areas carry no count; the chart for Rule 14.82 draws each region at its true size.
Private coverage includes plans through an employer, plans bought directly and TRICARE; public coverage includes Medicare, Medicaid and other means-tested plans, and VA care.
alt: Two overlapping circles inside a frame for everyone. Private coverage only, 189.4 million; both, 23.8 million; public coverage only, 95.4 million; and no coverage, outside both circles, 28.3 million.
notes_internal: Maker A, round 4. Data plan row 117, rule 14.81. Domain D09 (V7 I133). Draft before the data lead's rulings.
